capturePath.bounds: Capture accepts at most 16384 bytes per command and two exact-schema records; missing/oversized/invalid data stays partial without changing the original command result.

fixtureSemantics.lifecycle: One bounded 65537-byte read after fixture assertions/failure; oversized rejects data, retains at most 16 closed lifecycle events/time/ordinal generation. A missing event is not evidence it did not occur.
fixtureSemantics.existingFailureLogs: Existing sanitized failure log capture is unchanged; the new lifecycle output does not expose raw PID/log lines.

limits: All conclusions are source-level; no shell/Node/TypeScript/macOS execution, Actions raw-log read, artifact download, resource creation, branch publication or runtime success occurred in this review.
Adding synchronous instrumentation still changes timing. Non-reproduction of the formal EIO5 failure is not proof of a product fix and does not replace Node22 formal acceptance.
Completion means the observed command promise settled, including failures; an exit code, absent lifecycle line, or nonzero service probe does not prove process absence.
Author reported candidate commit/tree binding separately; this review independently fetched and recomputed all listed file blobs and manifest hashes, but did not reread the candidate commit tree.
After the sole actual run, root/diagnostic owner must preserve result and cleanup receipts and close the operational guards normally.
